296:             let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(c.origin.0, c.origin.1), seed, config);
297:             BuildOctreeUseCase::new(&DEFAULT_MATERIAL_PALETTE).execute(
298:                 &grid,
299:                 config.svo_depth(),
300:                 config.svo_world_size(),
301:             )
302:         })
303:         .collect();
304: 
305:     let ro = [5.0f32, 1.7, 5.0];
306:     let mut phantoms = Vec::new();
307:     let mut hit_count = 0usize;
308: 
309: 
310:     for yi in 0..64 {
311:         for pi in -8..=8i32 {
312:             let yaw = yi as f32 / 64.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
313:             let pitch = pi as f32 / 8.0 * 1.2;
314:             let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
315:             let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
316:             let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
317: 
318:             let Some(hit) = march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd) else {
319:                 continue;
320:             };
321:             hit_count += 1;
322: 
323: 
324:             let scale = config.voxel_scale;
325:             let c = [
326:                 (hit.box_min[0] + hit.box_max[0]) * 0.5,
327:                 (hit.box_min[1] + hit.box_max[1]) * 0.5,
328:                 (hit.box_min[2] + hit.box_max[2]) * 0.5,
329:             ];
330:             let (vx, vy, vz) = (
331:                 (c[0] / scale) as u32,
332:                 (c[1] / scale) as u32,
333:                 (c[2] / scale) as u32,
334:             );
335:             let truth = svos[hit.chunk].get(vx, vy, vz);
336:             let solid = truth.map(|(vt, _, _, _)| vt != 0).unwrap_or(false);
337:             if !solid {
338:                 phantoms.push((yaw, pitch, hit));
339:             }
340:         }
341:     }
342: 
343:     assert!(
344:         hit_count > 200,
345:         "sanity: the sweep must actually hit walls, got {hit_count}"
346:     );
347:     assert!(
348:         phantoms.is_empty(),
349:         "{} phantom hits out of {}; first 5: {:#?}",
350:         phantoms.len(),
351:         hit_count,
352:         &phantoms[..phantoms.len().min(5)]
353:     );
354: }

360: #[test]
361: fn pitched_rays_never_escape_through_cracks() {
362:     let seed = 42;
363:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
364:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
365: 
366:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
367:     for dz in -1..=1 {
368:         for dx in -1..=1 {
369:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
370:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
371:                 (ox, oz),
372:                 0,
373:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
374:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
375:             ));
376:         }
377:     }
378:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
379: 
380:     let mut misses = 0usize;
381:     let mut total = 0usize;
382:     for px in 0..8 {
383:         for pz in 0..8 {
384:             let ro = [1.0137 + px as f32 * 1.11, 1.7, 0.9713 + pz as f32 * 1.19];
385:             for yi in 0..128 {
386:                 for pi in [-40i32, -25, 25, 40] {
387:                     let yaw = (yi as f32 + 0.173) / 128.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
388:                     let pitch = pi as f32 / 60.0 * 1.2;
389:                     let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
390:                     let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
391:                     let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
392:                     total += 1;
393:                     if march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd).is_none() {
394:                         misses += 1;
395:                     }
396:                 }
397:             }
398:         }
399:     }
400:     assert_eq!(
401:         misses, 0,
402:         "{misses} of {total} pitched rays escaped through cracks"
403:     );
404: }

149: fn assert_fixture_geometry(scene: &RoomScene) {
150:     let voxels = scene.voxels();
151:     let mut emissive = Vec::new();
152:     for y in 0..voxels.height() {
153:         for z in 0..voxels.depth() {
154:             for x in 0..voxels.width() {
155:                 if EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&voxels.get(x, y, z)) {
156:                     emissive.push((x, y, z));
157:                 }
158:             }
159:         }
160:     }
161: 
162:     assert_eq!(emissive.len(), 1, "fixture must contain one emitter");
163:     let (x, y, z) = emissive[0];
164:     assert_eq!(voxels.get(x, y, z), VOXEL_LIGHT);
165:     assert!(y > 0);
166:     assert_eq!(
167:         voxels.get(x, y - 1, z),
168:         VOXEL_AIR,
169:         "panel underside must be exposed to room air"
170:     );
171:     assert_eq!(voxels.get(x - 1, y, z), VOXEL_CEILING);
172:     assert_eq!(voxels.get(x + 1, y, z), VOXEL_CEILING);
173:     assert_eq!(voxels.get(x, y, z - 1), VOXEL_CEILING);
174:     assert_eq!(voxels.get(x, y, z + 1), VOXEL_CEILING);
175: 
176:     for z in 0..voxels.depth() {
177:         for x in 0..voxels.width() {
178:             assert!(
179:                 !EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&voxels.get(x, 0, z)),
180:                 "floor voxel ({x}, 0, {z}) must not emit"
181:             );
182:         }
183:     }
184: }

186: fn assert_lit_room(renderer: &str, image: &RenderedImage) {
187:     assert_eq!((image.width, image.height), (WIDTH, HEIGHT));
188:     assert_eq!(image.rgba.len(), (WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4) as usize);
189: 
190:     let mut visible_pixels = 0usize;
191:     let mut fixture_pixels = 0usize;
192:     let mut brightest = (0u8, 0usize, [0u8; 3]);
193:     for (index, pixel) in image.rgba.chunks_exact(4).enumerate() {
194:         assert_eq!(pixel[3], 255, "{renderer} produced non-opaque output");
195:         if pixel[..3] != [0, 0, 0] {
196:             visible_pixels += 1;
197:         }
198:         let x = index % image.width as usize;
199:         let y = index / image.width as usize;
200:         let luminance =
201:             ((u16::from(pixel[0]) + u16::from(pixel[1]) + u16::from(pixel[2])) / 3) as u8;
202:         if luminance > brightest.0 {
203:             brightest = (luminance, index, [pixel[0], pixel[1], pixel[2]]);
204:         }
205:         let in_panel_window = x >= image.width as usize / 3
206:             && x <= image.width as usize * 2 / 3
207:             && y < image.height as usize / 3;
208:         if in_panel_window && pixel[0] >= 240 && pixel[1] >= 225 && pixel[2] >= 190 {
209:             fixture_pixels += 1;
210:         }
211:     }
212: 
213:     let pixel_count = (WIDTH * HEIGHT) as usize;
214:     assert!(
215:         visible_pixels > pixel_count / 20,
216:         "{renderer} failed to show the baked-lit room: {visible_pixels}/{pixel_count} visible pixels"
217:     );
218:     assert!(
219:         fixture_pixels > 0,
220:         "{renderer} failed to show the exposed fluorescent panel; brightest={brightest:?}"
221:     );
222: }

183:             &fixture.frame,
184:             &fixture.scene.chunks,
185:             cpu_settings,
186:         );
187:     });
188:     assert_non_clear_variation("cpu-present", &cpu_present);
189: }

191: fn create_vulkan_context() -> VulkanContext {
192:     let mut descriptor = wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle();
193:     descriptor.backends = wgpu::Backends::VULKAN;
194:     descriptor.flags =
195:         wgpu::InstanceFlags::debugging() | wgpu::InstanceFlags::STRICT_WEBGPU_COMPLIANCE;
196:     let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(descriptor);
197:     let adapter = pollster::block_on(instance.request_adapter(&wgpu::RequestAdapterOptions {
198:         power_preference: wgpu::PowerPreference::None,
199:         force_fallback_adapter: false,
200:         compatible_surface: None,
201:         apply_limit_buckets: false,
202:     }))
203:     .unwrap_or_else(|error| {
204:         panic!(
205:             "Vulkan renderer tests require a Vulkan 1.2+ adapter; install Mesa Lavapipe or expose a Vulkan device: {error}"
206:         )
207:     });
208:     let info = adapter.get_info();
209:     assert_eq!(
210:         info.backend,
211:         wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
212:         "test harness must never fall back from Vulkan; selected {info:?}"
213:     );
214:     eprintln!(
215:         "Vulkan test adapter: {} ({}, {})",
216:         info.name, info.driver, info.driver_info
217:     );
218: 
219:     let (device, queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
220:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-device"),
221:         required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),
222:         required_limits: wgpu::Limits::defaults(),
223:         ..Default::default()
224:     }))
225:     .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to create the Vulkan test device: {error}"));
226: 
227:     VulkanContext {
228:         _instance: instance,
229:         device,
230:         queue,
231:     }
232: }

234: fn deterministic_fixture() -> Fixture {

240:     let splat_mesh = build_surface_artifacts(&halo, voxel_size, 0, 1, RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT);

278: fn add_lateral_air_halo(source: &VoxelGrid) -> VoxelGrid {
279:     let mut halo = VoxelGrid::new(source.width() + 2, source.height(), source.depth() + 2);
280:     for z in 0..source.depth() {
281:         for y in 0..source.height() {
282:             for x in 0..source.width() {
283:                 halo.set(x + 1, y, z + 1, source.get(x, y, z));
284:                 halo.set_light_rgb(x + 1, y, z + 1, source.get_light_rgb(x, y, z));
285:             }
286:         }
287:     }
288:     halo
289: }

291: fn create_production_pipelines(gpu: &VulkanContext) -> ProductionPipelines {
292:     let validation = gpu.device.push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation);
293:     let frame = FrameResources::new(&gpu.device);
294:     let surface = SurfacePipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 16.0);
295:     let splat = SplatPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 16.0, 16_384);
296:     let mut raymarch = RaymarchPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 1);
297:     raymarch.configure(RaymarchRuntimeOptions::new(16.0, true, 4));
298:     let cpu_present = CpuPresentPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, WIDTH, HEIGHT);
299:     let supply_labels = SupplyLabelPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout());
300:     assert_validation_clean(&gpu.device, validation, "production pipeline creation");
301:     ProductionPipelines {
302:         frame,
303:         surface,
304:         splat,
305:         raymarch,
306:         cpu_present,
307:         supply_labels,
308:     }
309: }

468: fn render_offscreen(
469:     gpu: &VulkanContext,
470:     label: &str,
471:     draw: impl FnOnce(&mut wgpu::CommandEncoder, &wgpu::TextureView, &wgpu::TextureView),
472: ) -> Vec<u8> {
473:     let validation = gpu.device.push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation);
474:     let extent = wgpu::Extent3d {
475:         width: WIDTH,
476:         height: HEIGHT,
477:         depth_or_array_layers: 1,
478:     };
479:     let color = gpu.device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
480:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-color"),
481:         size: extent,
482:         mip_level_count: 1,
483:         sample_count: 1,
484:         dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
485:         format: TARGET_FORMAT,
486:         usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_SRC,
487:         view_formats: &[],
488:     });
489:     let depth = gpu.device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
490:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-depth"),
491:         size: extent,
492:         mip_level_count: 1,
493:         sample_count: 1,
494:         dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
495:         format: wgpu::TextureFormat::Depth32Float,
496:         usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT,
497:         view_formats: &[],
498:     });
499:     let color_view = color.create_view(&Default::default());
500:     let depth_view = depth.create_view(&Default::default());
501:     let readback = gpu.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
502:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-readback"),
503:         size: u64::from(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW * HEIGHT),
504:         usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST | wgpu::BufferUsages::MAP_READ,
505:         mapped_at_creation: false,
506:     });
507:     let mut encoder = gpu
508:         .device
509:         .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor { label: Some(label) });
510:     draw(&mut encoder, &color_view, &depth_view);
511:     encoder.copy_texture_to_buffer(
512:         color.as_image_copy(),
513:         wgpu::TexelCopyBufferInfo {
514:             buffer: &readback,
515:             layout: wgpu::TexelCopyBufferLayout {
516:                 offset: 0,
517:                 bytes_per_row: Some(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW),
518:                 rows_per_image: Some(HEIGHT),
519:             },
520:         },
521:         extent,
522:     );
523:     gpu.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
524:     let validation_result = validation.pop();
525: 
526:     let (mapped_tx, mapped_rx) = mpsc::channel();
527:     readback
528:         .slice(..)
529:         .map_async(wgpu::MapMode::Read, move |result| {
530:             mapped_tx.send(result).expect("map receiver remains alive");
531:         });
532:     gpu.device
533:         .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
534:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: device polling failed: {error}"));
535:     mapped_rx
536:         .recv()
537:         .expect("Vulkan map callback must run")
538:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: readback mapping failed: {error}"));
539: 
540:     let pixels = {
541:         let padded = readback
542:             .slice(..)
543:             .get_mapped_range()
544:             .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: mapped range is unavailable: {error}"));
545:         let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity((RGBA_BYTES_PER_ROW * HEIGHT) as usize);
546:         for row in padded.chunks_exact(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW as usize) {
547:             pixels.extend_from_slice(&row[..RGBA_BYTES_PER_ROW as usize]);
548:         }
549:         pixels
550:     };
551:     readback.unmap();
552:     if let Some(error) = pollster::block_on(validation_result) {
553:         panic!("{label}: WebGPU/Vulkan validation error: {error}");
554:     }
555:     pixels
556: }
557: 
558: fn assert_validation_clean(device: &wgpu::Device, validation: wgpu::ErrorScopeGuard, label: &str) {
559:     let result = validation.pop();
560:     device
561:         .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
562:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: device polling failed: {error}"));
563:     if let Some(error) = pollster::block_on(result) {
564:         panic!("{label}: WebGPU/Vulkan validation error: {error}");
565:     }
566: }
567: 
568: fn assert_non_clear_variation(label: &str, rgba: &[u8]) {
569:     assert_eq!(rgba.len(), (WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4) as usize);
570:     let first = &rgba[..3];
571:     let mut different_from_clear = 0usize;
572:     let mut min_luminance = u16::MAX;
573:     let mut max_luminance = 0u16;
574:     for pixel in rgba.chunks_exact(4) {
575:         assert_eq!(pixel[3], 255, "{label} emitted non-opaque pixels");
576:         different_from_clear += usize::from(&pixel[..3] != first);
577:         let luminance = u16::from(pixel[0]) + u16::from(pixel[1]) + u16::from(pixel[2]);
578:         min_luminance = min_luminance.min(luminance);
579:         max_luminance = max_luminance.max(luminance);
580:     }
581:     assert!(
582:         different_from_clear > 8,
583:         "{label} remained at its clear color: first={first:?}, changed={different_from_clear}"
584:     );
585:     assert!(
586:         max_luminance.saturating_sub(min_luminance) > 6,
587:         "{label} produced no meaningful scene contrast: min={min_luminance}, max={max_luminance}"
588:     );
589: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/Cargo.toml
````toml
  1: # wasm_frontend — the browser front end of the voxel engine.
  2: #
  3: # Clean Architecture placement:
  4: #   application/  Use-case layer for the interactive client (player physics,
  5: #                 chunk streaming policy, frame orchestration). Pure Rust,
  6: #                 unit-tested natively. Defines the ports (RendererPort,
  7: #                 ChunkSourcePort) that outer layers implement.
  8: #   adapters/     Interface adapters: input mapping, SVO atlas assembly, and
  9: #                 the local chunk source that drives the `vackrooms` core
 10: #                 use cases (generation -> collision SVO -> renderer-selected
 11: #                 presentation artifacts).
 12: #   drivers/      Frameworks & Drivers: portable WebGPU pipelines plus browser
 13: #                 surface/event/rAF plumbing. DOM-facing code is wasm-only;
 14: #                 native Vulkan tests execute the same pipeline modules.
 15: [package]
 16: name = "wasm_frontend"
 17: version = "0.1.0"
 18: edition = "2024"
 19: 
 20: [lib]
 21: crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
 22: 
 23: [features]
 24: vulkan-tests = []
 25: 
 26: [[test]]
 27: name = "vulkan_renderers"
 28: path = "tests/vulkan_renderers.rs"
 29: required-features = ["vulkan-tests"]
 30: 
 31: [dependencies]
 32: bytemuck = { version = "1.25", features = ["derive"] }
 33: image = { version = "0.25.10", default-features = false, features = ["png"] }
 34: vackrooms = { path = ".." }
 35: 
 36: # Keep the portable renderer pipelines buildable on the host. Native tests
 37: # select Vulkan explicitly and render into headless textures; the `play`
 38: # binary opens a real window through winit.
 39: [target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
 40: wgpu = { version = "30.0", default-features = false, features = ["std", "vulkan", "wgsl"] }
 41: winit = "0.30"
 42: pollster = "1.0"
 43: # Rasterizes the vendored Bytesized face into the native HUD glyph atlas.
 44: fontdue = "0.9"
 45: 
 46: # Browser bindings are wasm-only so `cargo test` on the host runs the pure
 47: # application/adapters layers without pulling in web-sys.
 48: [target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
 49: wasm-bindgen = "0.2"

 51: console_error_panic_hook = "0.1"

 53: wgpu = { version = "30.0", default-features = false, features = ["std", "webgpu", "wgsl"] }
 54: web-sys = { version = "0.3", features = [

 65:     "MouseEvent",
 66:     "TouchEvent",
 67:     "TouchList",
 68:     "Touch",
 69:     "Navigator",
 70:     "Performance",
 71:     "Worker",
 72:     "WorkerOptions",
 73:     "WorkerType",
 74:     "MessageEvent",
 75:     "console",
 76:     "Storage",
 77:     "CanvasRenderingContext2d",
 78:     "ImageData",
 79:     "WebGl2RenderingContext",
 80:     "WebGlProgram",
 81:     "WebGlQuery",

  1: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
  2: 
  3: const VOXEL_AIR: u8 = 0;
  4: const VOXEL_LIGHT: u8 = 4;
  5: 
  6: #[wasm_bindgen]
  7: pub struct CPURaycaster {
  8:     grid_data: Vec<u8>,
  9:     light_data: Vec<u8>,
 10:     width: usize,
 11:     height: usize,
 12:     depth: usize,
 13:     frame_buffer: Vec<u8>,
 14:     screen_width: usize,
 15:     screen_height: usize,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: #[wasm_bindgen]
 19: impl CPURaycaster {
 20:     #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
 21:     pub fn new(screen_width: usize, screen_height: usize) -> Self {
 22:         Self {
 23:             grid_data: Vec::new(),
 24:             light_data: Vec::new(),
 25:             width: 0,
 26:             height: 0,
 27:             depth: 0,
 28:             frame_buffer: vec![255; screen_width * screen_height * 4],
 29:             screen_width,
 30:             screen_height,
 31:         }
 32:     }
 33: 
 34:     pub fn set_grid(
 35:         &mut self,
 36:         width: usize,
 37:         height: usize,
 38:         depth: usize,
 39:         data: &[u8],
 40:         light: &[u8],
 41:     ) {
 42:         self.width = width;
 43:         self.height = height;
 44:         self.depth = depth;
 45:         self.grid_data = data.to_vec();
 46:         self.light_data = light.to_vec();
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     pub fn get_frame_buffer(&self) -> *const u8 {
 50:         self.frame_buffer.as_ptr()
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     fn get_voxel(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 54:         if x < 0
 55:             || y < 0
 56:             || z < 0
 57:             || x >= self.width as isize
 58:             || y >= self.height as isize
 59:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 60:         {
 61:             return VOXEL_AIR;
 62:         }
 63:         self.grid_data
 64:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     fn get_light(&self, x: isize, y: isize, z: isize) -> u8 {
 68:         if x < 0
 69:             || y < 0
 70:             || z < 0
 71:             || x >= self.width as isize
 72:             || y >= self.height as isize
 73:             || z >= self.depth as isize
 74:         {
 75:             return 0;
 76:         }
 77:         self.light_data
 78:             [(y as usize * self.width * self.depth) + (z as usize * self.width) + (x as usize)]
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     pub fn render(&mut self, px: f32, py: f32, pz: f32, yaw: f32, pitch: f32, fov_deg: f32) {
 82: 
 83:         for i in (0..self.frame_buffer.len()).step_by(4) {
 84:             self.frame_buffer[i] = 10;
 85:             self.frame_buffer[i + 1] = 10;
 86:             self.frame_buffer[i + 2] = 10;
 87:             self.frame_buffer[i + 3] = 255;
 88:         }
 89: 
 90:         if self.width == 0 {
 91:             return;
 92:         }
 93: 
 94:         let fov_rad = fov_deg * std::f32::consts::PI / 180.0;
 95:         let half_fov = fov_rad / 2.0;
 96: 
 97:         let dir_x = -yaw.sin();
 98:         let dir_z = -yaw.cos();
 99:         let plane_x = yaw.cos() * half_fov.tan();
100:         let plane_z = -yaw.sin() * half_fov.tan();
101: 
102:         for x in 0..self.screen_width {
103:             let camera_x = 2.0 * (x as f32) / (self.screen_width as f32) - 1.0;
104:             let ray_dir_x = dir_x + plane_x * camera_x;
105:             let ray_dir_z = dir_z + plane_z * camera_x;
106: 
107:             let mut map_x = px.floor() as isize;
108:             let mut map_z = pz.floor() as isize;
109: 
110:             let delta_dist_x = if ray_dir_x == 0.0 {
111:                 f32::INFINITY
112:             } else {
113:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_x).abs()
114:             };
115:             let delta_dist_z = if ray_dir_z == 0.0 {
116:                 f32::INFINITY
117:             } else {
118:                 (1.0 / ray_dir_z).abs()
119:             };
120: 
121:             let mut side_dist_x;
122:             let mut side_dist_z;
123:             let step_x: isize;
124:             let step_z: isize;
125: 
126:             if ray_dir_x < 0.0 {
127:                 step_x = -1;
128:                 side_dist_x = (px - map_x as f32) * delta_dist_x;
129:             } else {
130:                 step_x = 1;
131:                 side_dist_x = (map_x as f32 + 1.0 - px) * delta_dist_x;
132:             }
133: 
134:             if ray_dir_z < 0.0 {
135:                 step_z = -1;
136:                 side_dist_z = (pz - map_z as f32) * delta_dist_z;
137:             } else {
138:                 step_z = 1;
139:                 side_dist_z = (map_z as f32 + 1.0 - pz) * delta_dist_z;
140:             }
141: 
142:             let mut hit = 0;
143:             let mut side = 0;
144:             let mut perp_wall_dist = 0.0;
145:             let mut hit_y = 0;
146: 
147:             let map_y = py.floor() as isize;
148:             let max_steps = 200;
149:             let mut steps = 0;
150: 
151:             while hit == 0 && steps < max_steps {
152:                 if side_dist_x < side_dist_z {
153:                     side_dist_x += delta_dist_x;
154:                     map_x += step_x;
155:                     side = 0;
156:                 } else {
157:                     side_dist_z += delta_dist_z;
158:                     map_z += step_z;
159:                     side = 1;
160:                 }
161: 
162:                 let v = self.get_voxel(map_x, map_y, map_z);
163:                 if v != VOXEL_AIR {
164:                     hit = v;
165:                     hit_y = map_y;
166:                 }
167:                 steps += 1;
168:             }
169: 
170:             if hit > 0 {
171:                 if side == 0 {
172:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_x - delta_dist_x;
173:                 } else {
174:                     perp_wall_dist = side_dist_z - delta_dist_z;
175:                 }
176: 
177:                 let line_height = (self.screen_height as f32 / perp_wall_dist).abs() as isize;
178:                 let pitch_offset = (pitch * self.screen_height as f32) as isize;
179: 
180:                 let mut draw_start =
181:                     -line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
182:                 let draw_start_clamped = if draw_start < 0 {
183:                     0
184:                 } else {
185:                     draw_start as usize
186:                 };
187:                 let mut draw_end = line_height / 2 + self.screen_height as isize / 2 + pitch_offset;
188:                 if draw_end >= self.screen_height as isize {
189:                     draw_end = self.screen_height as isize - 1;
190:                 }
191:                 let draw_end_clamped = draw_end as usize;
192: 
193:                 let mut r = 200;
194:                 let mut g = 200;
195:                 let mut b = 200;
196: 
197:                 if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
198:                     r = 255;
199:                     g = 255;
200:                     b = 200;
201:                 } else if hit == 5 {
202:                     r = 150;
203:                     g = 30;
204:                     b = 30;
205:                 } else if hit == 1 {
206:                     r = 180;
207:                     g = 160;
208:                     b = 100;
209:                 }
210: 
211:                 let light = self.get_light(map_x, hit_y, map_z);
212:                 let light_factor = if hit == VOXEL_LIGHT {
213:                     1.0
214:                 } else {
215:                     light as f32 / 15.0
216:                 };
217:                 let fog_factor = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.05).exp();
218: 
219:                 r = (r as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
220:                 g = (g as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
221:                 b = (b as f32 * light_factor * fog_factor) as u8;
222: 
223:                 if side == 1 && hit != VOXEL_LIGHT {
224:                     r = (r as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
225:                     g = (g as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
226:                     b = (b as f32 * 0.7) as u8;
227:                 }
228: 
229:                 for y in draw_start_clamped..=draw_end_clamped {
230:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
231:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = r;
232:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = g;
233:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = b;
234:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
235:                 }
236: 
237:                 let floor_fog = (-perp_wall_dist * 0.01).exp();
238:                 for y in (draw_end_clamped + 1)..self.screen_height {
239:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
240:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
241:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
242:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (40.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
243:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
244:                 }
245: 
246:                 for y in 0..draw_start_clamped {
247:                     let pixel_idx = (y * self.screen_width + x) * 4;
248:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx] = (60.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
249:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 1] = (55.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
250:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 2] = (50.0 * floor_fog) as u8;
251:                     self.frame_buffer[pixel_idx + 3] = 255;
252:                 }
253:             }
254:         }
255:     }
256: }
````

## File: Cargo.toml
````toml
 1: # Workspace root. Layout:
 2: #   .              -> `vackrooms` core: Entities + Use Cases + Interface Adapters,
 3: #                     plus the native dev server binary (Frameworks & Drivers).
 4: #                     The library is platform-agnostic and also compiles to wasm32.
 5: #   wasm_frontend  -> Four portable WebGPU strategies plus the wasm browser
 6: #                     shell; the same pipelines run headlessly on Vulkan/
 7: #                     Lavapipe in CI.
 8: #   wasm_raycaster -> Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (kept for reference).
 9: [workspace]
10: members = [".", "wasm_frontend", "wasm_raycaster"]
11: 
12: [package]
13: name = "vackrooms"
14: version = "0.1.0"
15: edition = "2024"
16: 
17: [dependencies]
18: # default-features disabled so the `os_rng`/getrandom backend is never pulled in;
19: # every RNG in the engine is deterministically seeded (StdRng::seed_from_u64),
20: # which keeps the core buildable on wasm32-unknown-unknown.
21: rand = { version = "0.10.2", default-features = false, features = ["std", "std_rng"] }
22: 
23: [dev-dependencies]
24: criterion = "0.8"
25: 
26: [[bench]]
27: name = "generation"
28: harness = false
````

## File: README.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only engine in Rust, organized with Clean Architecture and compiled
  4: to WebAssembly. Procedural world planning, finite-range voxel irradiance,
  5: sparse voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, and sliding player
  6: collision remain deterministic CPU work. One WebGPU facade presents four
  7: runtime-selectable strategies: indexed surfaces, compact face splats, SVO
  8: raymarching, and a CPU reference image uploaded through WebGPU.
  9: 
 10: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design (layer map, ports,
 11: data flow, SVO node encoding, streaming, and rendering pipelines).
 12: 
 13: ## How it works
 14: 
 15: Each chunk starts with the same authoritative pipeline, on the main thread or
 16: in a generation worker. The selected renderer controls which derived upload
 17: artifacts are retained:
 18: 
 19: 1. **Procedural generation** (`src/use_cases/generate_chunk.rs` +
 20:    `*_level.rs`) — a `LevelGenerator` fills a `VoxelGrid` deterministically
 21:    from `(chunk position, seed, config)`. Level 0 is the office backrooms;
 22:    level 34 is an open grassland. Both tile seamlessly because geometry is
 23:    derived from world-space coordinates, never chunk-local ones.
 24: 2. **Lighting preparation** — exposed emissive faces seed an air-only,
 25:    finite-range RGB diffuse field; solids receive it but never propagate it.
 26:    Runtime panels are separately derived from exposed emissive undersides and
 27:    remain analytic area lights in every renderer strategy.
 28: 3. **SVO build + optional serialization** — the lit grid is packed into a
 29:    sparse voxel octree for collision and traversal. Recursive cubes wholly
 30:    beyond a non-power-of-two grid are pruned directly to the canonical air
 31:    leaf. Raymarch and CPU strategies serialize nodes as a row-padded,
 32:    four-`u32` stream; raymarch uploads it to GPU storage while the CPU
 33:    reference decodes the same words (`src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`).
 34: 4. **Streaming** (`wasm_frontend/src/application/streaming.rs`) — chunks
 35:    around the player are requested, LOD'd by distance, and evicted as the
 36:    player moves; a coarse-first pass keeps distant chunks cheap.
 37: 5. **Collision** — player movement is axis-separated (X and Z tested and
 38:    moved independently against a `CollisionWorld`), so hitting a wall
 39:    diagonally slides along it instead of stopping dead.
 40: 6. **Render** — one `WebGpuRenderer` port adapter delegates resident chunks to
 41:    one of four composable strategies (see below).
 42: 
 43: Generation is deliberately CPU-authoritative: architectural graph decisions,
 44: reality epochs, and seeded noise must produce the same chunk regardless of
 45: GPU or worker scheduling. The GPU instead performs renderer-derived work that
 46: does not redefine the world: vertex pulling, face-to-quad expansion,
 47: depth-tested supply-label billboard expansion, and per-pixel SVO traversal.
 48: 
 49: A standing gameplay quirk: leaning into a wall for a few seconds has a
 50: chance to "noclip" the player between level 0 (backrooms) and level 34
 51: (grassland) — see `update_noclip` in
 52: `wasm_frontend/src/application/engine.rs`.
 53: 
 54: ### Renderer backends
 55: 
 56: Chosen with `?renderer=` (see [Usage](#usage)):
 57: 
 58: | Value | WebGPU strategy | Notes |
 59: |---|---|---|
 60: | `surface` *(default)* | indexed surfaces | Greedy-mesh indices plus compact vertices. WGSL pulls and decodes vertices from a storage buffer; hardware depth resolves visibility. |
 61: | `splat` | face splats | Compact face records live in a storage buffer. The vertex stage expands each record into four corners; CPU draw submission applies the configured cell and face budgets. |
 62: | `raymarch` | SVO raymarcher | A fullscreen triangle drives fragment-stage traversal of the merged SVO storage-buffer atlas. |
 63: | `cpu` | CPU reference / WebGPU present | The deterministic software SVO rasterizer writes RGBA8; WebGPU uploads that framebuffer to a texture and presents it. |
 64: 
 65: All four choices require WebGPU for presentation. Adapter or device creation
 66: failure is reported in the loading HUD; the engine does not silently switch
 67: rendering algorithms.
 68: 
 69: ## Build & run
 70: 
 71: Prerequisites: Rust (with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target) and
 72: [`wasm-pack`](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/).
 73: The page imports wasm-bindgen's native ES-module output directly; there is no
 74: webpack build stage in this repository.
 75: 
 76: ```sh
 77: # 1. Build the wasm front end into static/pkg/
 78: npm run build:wasm
 79: 
 80: # 2. Run the dev server
 81: cargo run
 82: 
 83: # 3. Open http://localhost:3000
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: ## Usage
 87: 
 88: Click to capture the mouse; WASD to move, ESC to release.
 89: 
 90: - `http://localhost:3000/` — wasm engine (low-spec profile: 3×3 chunk
 91:   streaming, 0.2 u voxels, adaptive resolution)
 92: - `http://localhost:3000/?spec=high` — high-spec profile (5×5 chunks,
 93:   0.1 u voxels)
 94: 
 95: The former `/legacy` Three.js client and route have been retired. The native
 96: server still exposes `/maze` and `/octree` as diagnostic data endpoints; the
 97: wasm client does not depend on them.
 98: 
 99: Worlds are shareable by URL — every query parameter below is optional and
100: combinable:
101: 
102: | Parameter | Values | Effect |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `spec` | `low`, `high` | Shared generation/rendering quality decision (case-insensitive). Default is low. |
105: | `voxel_size` | `0.4`, `0.2`, `0.1`, `0.05` | Overrides scene voxel size after seam, progressive-LOD, SVO-depth, and dense-memory validation. `0.4` is high-profile-only; `0.05` is standard-profile-only. |
106: | `seed` | number or text | World seed. Non-numeric text is hashed (FNV-1a) so words work too. |
107: | `pillars` | `0`–`4` | Structural column density multiplier (`0` = none). Default `1`. |
108: | `walls` | `0`–`4` | Office wall density multiplier (`0` = open plan). Default `1`. |
109: | `atria` | `0`–`4` | How much of the world vaults into tall atria. Default `1`. |
110: | `lights` | `0`–`4` | Ceiling light panel density. Default `1`. |
111: | `renderer` | `surface`, `splat`, `raymarch`, `cpu` | Selects one of the four WebGPU strategies (see above). |
112: | `cpu_preset` | `performance`, `balanced`, `quality`, `maximum`, `custom` | Typed CPU workload profile. Presets render at 12.5%–50% backing resolution per axis and present the complete image over the full page; `balanced` is the default. |
113: | `cpu_scale` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom CPU backing scale relative to the 25%-viewport baseline; CSS presentation always remains full-page. |
114: | `cpu_lod_px` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom projected-radius MIP cutoff; lower preserves finer distant geometry. |
115: | `cpu_splat_radius_px` | `1`–`16` | Custom maximum splat radius; lower values virtually split large leaves for finer surfaces. |
116: | `cpu_virtual_depth` | `3`–`8` | Custom cap on virtual solid-leaf subdivision. |
117: | `cpu_mip_occupancy` | `0`–`0.5` | Custom sparse-LOD rejection threshold; lower retains sparser distant detail. |
118: | `cpu_range` | `16`–`256` | CPU draw distance in world units. |
119: | `cpu_shadows` | `off`, `hero`, `full` | CPU fixture visibility: unshadowed, one cached hero-fixture approximation, or the expensive reference that traces every point/Gauss-sample endpoint. |
120: | `workers` | `auto`, `0`, `1`–`4` | Chunk-generation/streaming concurrency. `auto` reserves the main thread and uses at most four workers; explicit counts clamp to reported hardware. `0` uses the synchronous main-thread fallback. This does not parallelize rendering. |
121: | `level` | `0`, `34` | Debug: boots straight into a level (34 = the grassland) instead of waiting on a noclip roll. |
122: | `force_anomaly` | `pillars`, `blackout`, `pits`, `archway`, `redroom` | Debug: guarantees one anomaly of that family near spawn, bypassing organic frequency and the spawn keep-out. |
123: | `rt_hiz` | `0`, `1` | CPU hierarchical-Z rejection. |
124: | `rt_f2b` | `0`, `1` | CPU traversal plus splat/raymarch near-to-far chunk selection. Off preserves each strategy's deterministic reference order. |
125: | `rt_skip` | `0`, `1` | Raymarch empty-SVO-leaf skipping; `0` selects finest-cell diagnostic DDA. |
126: | `rt_mips` | `0`, `1` | CPU projected-size MIP/LOD collapse. |
127: | `rt_beam_occlusion` | `0`, `1` | CPU cone-light occlusion rays. |
128: | `rt_deferred` | `0`, `1` | CPU exact fine-depth rejection before hidden-splat shading. Off shades first and depth-tests later; pixels are identical. |
129: | `rt_ao` | `0`, `1` | CPU sibling-count ambient-occlusion approximation. Off selects unit ambient visibility for the reference path. |
130: | `rt_shadows` | `0`, `1` | Direct-light visibility. Surface/Splat use a hero-fixture depth map (128² hard comparison on low, 256² four-tap PCF on high); raymarch traces finite SVO segments to each point-light endpoint and one/four rectangle samples. |
131: | `rt_cells` | `0`, `1` | CPU-side splat cell-range rejection before direct draw submission. |
132: | `rt_budget` | `0`, `1` | Splat far-chunk face budget. |
133: | `rt_cull` | `0`, `1` | CPU and all WebGPU strategies reject chunks beyond the configured range; raster strategies also apply conservative camera visibility. Raymarch filters complete chunk bounds before its resident-set cap. |
134: | `rt_dither` | `0`, `1` | Shared WebGPU output dither. |
135: | `rt_bake` | `0`, `1` | Optional quantized diffuse fill for CPU, surface, and splat; raymarch remains analytic. |
136: 
137: The top-right HUD names the section you are in (level, zone, region), and
138: **F3** (or Settings → Debug) toggles the anomaly debug overlay: reality
139: epochs, resident traversal gates and pit hazards, and streaming counters.
140: 
141: The in-page settings menu (gear icon) also exposes mouse sensitivity, invert
142: Y, render scale, FOV, control scheme, typed CPU quality presets/custom detail,
143: and every renderer optimization switch. CPU quality scalars do not silently
144: change optimization switches: hierarchical Z, MIP collapse, traversal order,
145: chunk culling, hidden-splat rejection, ambient occlusion, and flashlight scene-visibility rays remain independently
146: diagnosable. Older `cpuScale`, `cpuSplatPx`, `cpuRange`, and `cpuShadows` links
147: are still accepted; the formerly ambiguous `cpuSplatPx` is interpreted as a
148: radius.
149: Live preferences are saved to `localStorage`; Apply & Reload writes disabled
150: optimizations into the URL so a regression setup can be shared exactly.
151: 
152: ## GitHub Pages
153: 
154: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds `wasm_frontend` in release mode and
155: deploys `static/` on every push to `master` (or via manual dispatch). The
156: main engine (`/`, low- and high-spec profiles) generates chunks entirely in
157: the browser, so it needs nothing but static files and runs unmodified from a
158: Pages project URL (`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) — the worker pool
159: resolves `worker.js` relative to the page, not from the domain root.
160: 
161: The optional `/maze` and `/octree` diagnostics belong to `src/main.rs` and
162: are absent on Pages; the wasm engine needs neither endpoint.
163: 
164: One-time setup: in the repo's Settings → Pages, set Source to "GitHub
165: Actions".
166: 
167: ## Tests
168: 
169: ```sh
170: cargo test --workspace
171: cargo check -p wasm_frontend --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
172: npm run check:wasm
173: 
174: # Linux: deterministic headless GPU contracts through Vulkan/Lavapipe.
175: VK_DRIVER_FILES="$(find /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d -name 'lvp_icd*.json' -print -quit)" \
176:   WGPU_VALIDATION=1 \
177:   cargo test -p wasm_frontend --features vulkan-tests \
178:     --test vulkan_renderers -- --test-threads=1
179: ```
180: 
181: The application layers are browser-free by construction, so player physics,
182: collision, streaming, atlas assembly and input mapping are all covered by
183: native unit tests. The Vulkan suite uses a surface-free render target, forces
184: the Vulkan backend, and fails if no Vulkan adapter is available; CI pins it to
185: Mesa's deterministic Lavapipe software driver and enables Vulkan validation
186: layers. The exact Lavapipe ICD filename varies by distribution; CI discovers
187: it under `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/` before running the suite.
188: 
189: `npm run build:wasm` also writes a source fingerprint into `static/pkg/`.
190: `npm run check:wasm` verifies that the checked-in wasm-bindgen glue matches
191: the current Rust and worker ABI, catching stale worker-call signatures without
192: bringing a browser automation dependency back into the project.
193: 
194: ## Workspace layout
195: 
196: | Path | What it is |
197: |---|---|
198: | `src/` | `vackrooms` core: entities, use cases, adapters + native dev server |
199: | `wasm_frontend/` | Portable application/adapters/WebGPU pipelines plus the wasm browser shell |
200: | `static/` | Thin HTML shell and wasm bundle output (`pkg/`) |
201: | `wasm_raycaster/` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (reference only) |
202: 
203: ## Modifying the engine
204: 
205: Ports (traits) sit at the boundary of each layer; implement the trait rather
206: than reaching into a concrete type:
207: 
208: - **New procedural level** — implement `LevelGenerator`
209:   (`src/use_cases/level_generator.rs`) alongside `backrooms_level.rs` /
210:   `grassland_level.rs`, register a level id, and give it a native unit test
211:   (generation must be deterministic and seamless at chunk borders — see the
212:   contract documented on the trait).
213: - **New renderer strategy** — add a focused pipeline under
214:   `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/pipelines/`, give it typed configuration
215:   and artifact requirements in `webgpu/config.rs`, then compose it inside the
216:   single `WebGpuRenderer` port adapter. Browser surface ownership stays out of
217:   the pipeline.
218: - **New chunk source** (e.g. a different streaming/caching strategy) —
219:   implement `ChunkSourcePort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`); see
220:   `LocalChunkSource` and `WorkerChunkSource` for the synchronous and
221:   worker-pool implementations.
222: - **Player/physics tuning** — `wasm_frontend/src/application/player.rs` and
223:   `engine.rs`; both are plain Rust, unit-tested natively without a browser.
224: 
225: After changing anything under `src/` or `wasm_frontend/src/`, run
226: `cargo test --workspace` (native, browser-free) before rebuilding the wasm
227: bundle with the command in [Build & run](#build--run). See
228: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layer map and data flow.
````
